summary: The change does what the request asked. docs/spec.toml now has 264 active requirements. I counted them, and the count matches the raised floor in both xtask/tests/spec.rs and the Hestia test. Every heading of BRIEF.md that has text under it, including every dated addendum, is now the first source heading of some requirement. Three cases the request named: OLY-A-32 cites 2026-10-12 "Chunking and parallel work", the existing OLY-A-22 cites 2026-10-13 "Athena owns acceleration", and OLY-B-GOAL-05 quotes "measurably faster, cheaper, and more correct". In the spec test, `coverage_gaps` is now one general rule over the whole brief, replacing the old list of special cases. Headings with nothing under them are exempt only through a pinned list that a test checks. New negative tests remove the requirements for A6, the 2026-10-12 chunking addendum, a 2026-10-26 addendum, Goal and "How I'll judge it", and each asserts that exactly that heading is reported. With the old code they would fail, because it never looked at A6, Goal or the pre-Olympus addenda. Eight new open questions (OQ-4 to OQ-11) quote both sides of a conflict, and none resolves it. CHANGELOG.md has an entry. Every changed file is on the expected deliverables list. I ran the spec test (30 passed), the boundary scan (12 passed) and the Hestia test that reads the real spec (passed). fmt, clippy and the full test suite passed in Athena's recorded checks. I found two minor problems: a comment in spec.toml that is now out of date, and the Who's who section, which the brief says Olympus replaces but which the spec lists as active with no note.
